title: A linear recovery clock gives a poor fit to five ASASSN-14ko Swift cycles under a two-state count model
abstract: We test the recovery edge of the constant ASASSN-14ko X-ray clock. We use 193 published Swift visits in five clean-ingress cycles and extend each window to 100 days after ingress. A two-state negative-binomial model gives recovery times of 8.66 and 6.61 days in cycles 20 and 21, and 86.97 and 83.73 days in cycles 30 and 31. Cycle 33 has no observed recovery. A nonnegative affine duration law, as required by one unreset high-depth circular sector in its short-edge limit, loses 43.99 in twice log likelihood against separate durations at fixed count shape k=5. At k=2 the loss is 20.73. Slow recovery edges weaken the result. The test assumes an equal pre-dip and post-dip on level within each cycle, fixed ingress phases and independent count fluctuations. It does not exclude regenerated or slowly clearing screens, hybrid intrinsic low states, correlated AGN noise, or all obscuration. It does not measure a stellar orbital period. Original code, aggregate results, numerical checks, a conditional simulation calibration and source hashes are supplied. External observation records stay outside the package.

display.caption: Swift soft counts and fitted recovery times. Separate-duration curves omit censored cycle 33. The affine recovery law sacrifices the short early dips. Error bars show count scale, not source flicker.
